messages:
Maria: quick heads up — I have a small reproducible failure when bundling the JS SDK for an edge sample app. Behavior: first request succeeds, token refresh runs, subsequent requests get 401 and SDK keeps retrying (auth/retry loop).
Alex: can you drop the minimal repro steps and a short snippet?
Maria: yes. repro uses vite (v4) + swc plugin, target="edge". Install and build steps:
```
npm init -y
npm i @redwood-inference/sdk vite @swc/core vite-plugin-swc
# sample src/main.ts uses the SDK
vite build --ssr
# run edge runner (esbuild-ish runtime) or deploy to local edge shim
```
Minimal code: src/main.ts
```
import RedwoodSDK from '@redwood-inference/sdk';
const client = new RedwoodSDK({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY });
export default async function handler(req) {
  const r = await client.generate({ prompt: 'hi' });
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(r));
}
```
When bundling, Vite/rollup resolution selects the CJS entry (package.json main) for the packaged SDK. That ends up inlining a require-based auth util that uses `module.exports =` style. The edge ESM runtime sees a namespace object and our SDK's header attach code does `import util from './auth'` style, so the default vs namespace mismatch means the auth header function is undefined at runtime — token refresh runs but headers are lost on retry.
Sam: hmm, so it's not Vite per se, it's the main/module field precedence. Does setting resolve.mainFields to ['module','main'] change it?
Maria: exactly — forcing module first fixes it. But not all templates set that, and many users rely on default bundler behavior. Repro also fails under rollup when commonjs plugin runs and converts ESM -> CJS.
Jules: can you paste the stack snippet?
Maria: stack is short: `TypeError: attachAuthHeader is not a function` at auth-wrap (sdk/dist/cjs/auth.js:12) -> handler. Also TS intellisense shows `attachAuthHeader: any` missing named export.
Alex: two follow-ups — 1) add a note in DX docs about bundler mainFields for edge builds; 2) push a tiny change to SDK publish: add a top-level `exports` map with `import`/`require` so bundlers prefer ESM. That should prevent CJS inlining.
Sam: I'll try a quick patch: in vite.config.ts add
```
export default defineConfig({
  resolve: { mainFields: ['module', 'main'] },
  optimizeDeps: { exclude: ['@redwood-inference/sdk'] }
});
```
and see if optimizer still confuses it.
Maria: optimizeDeps exclude helped during dev but build still picks wrong entry if exports missing. Workaround for sampleapp: `alias: { '@redwood-inference/sdk': path.resolve('node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/esm/index.js') }` — gross but works.
Jules: for types: we need to ensure index.d.ts uses `export * from './types'; export { default } from './dist/esm/index';` or a clear type-only entry. Current `export =` shape breaks consumers expecting default export.
CI Bot: added a failing smoke test to the sampleapp pipeline referencing this repro — build step now fails consistently on main branch. See pipeline 5892.
Alex: ok, action items: Sam to prototype package.json exports fix + types fix; Maria to add reproducible minimal sample in /examples/vite-edge-auth-repro; Jules to author a short doc note for bundler pitfalls and recommended resolve config; I'll follow up on adding a unit test to SDK publish CI to verify exports map.
Sam: picking this up now. assigning to myself and will open PR with tests.
Maria: thanks — tagging eng-devex and eng-runtime for visibility. :thumbsup:
Alex: FYI, this is probably why a few support tickets about auth loops on edge customers popped up last week.
Maria: filing issue #1234 with the repro and snippets.
Sam: quick note — also check tree-shaking differences: ensure auth util is exported as named export in ESM bundles so default/namespace mismatch cannot occur.
Jules: noted. we'll also add a tiny sentence in the onboarding guide: "If deploying to edge runtimes with bundlers, prefer module-first resolution or ensure SDK's exports map is present."
Maria: perfect. thanks everyone.
